topics.topic: How confirmation bindings must guarantee distinction despite digest collisions
questions: Which guarantee must change: must digest collisions be excluded from admissible histories, or must collision-disambiguating information be retained so that different arguments are always distinguished?

The prompt must either exclude digest collisions from admissible histories or replace the digest-only binding with an injective or collision-disambiguating representation; collision resistance alone cannot guarantee that all different arguments have different digests.
Must the second passage be weakened to permit cryptographic collisions, or must admissible histories explicitly exclude collisions?

quotes: _confirmation_binding_digest: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST answer the hexadecimal text of a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous serialisation of the action, then the target, then the version, then every field of inputs in the order its model declares them, lists in the order given and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that equal arguments always give equal digests and different ones different digests;
MUST answer the hexadecimal text of a collision-resistant cryptographic digest
judgement.why: A collision-resistant digest can have collisions, while the same obligation requires every pair of different arguments to have different digests, so both requirements cannot hold for all admissible inputs unless collisions are explicitly excluded or additional distinguishing information is retained.
